sentences: We are standing before Rembrandt's The Night Watch.
Across a canvas more than four meters wide, an Amsterdam civic militia company is about to set off.
Pikes, a drumbeat and moving bodies seem to rush toward us at once.
Rembrandt finished it in 1642.
The captain and members of his company commissioned it for the great hall of their militia headquarters.
Group portraits of the time usually lined everyone up so each face got equal space.
Rembrandt broke with that custom and chose a moment of movement.
Captain Frans Banninck Cocq, in black with a red sash, strides forward as he gives the order, and the company begins to move around him.
Beside him, in yellow, is Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch.
The shadow of the captain's hand falls across his coat, with Amsterdam's coat of arms between thumb and fingers.
The city, it suggests, is safe in the militia's hands.
Now find the glowing girl on the left.
She shines out of the dark crowd on her own, with a dead chicken hanging at her waist.
Its claw was the emblem of this militia, the arquebusiers.
Next to her, the man in red is loading his musket.
Rembrandt spread three stages of handling a gun across the scene: loading, firing and cleaning.
It is a portrait and a piece of action at the same time.
Up in the middle, half hidden between other heads, a face peeks out of the crowd.
It is thought to be Rembrandt himself, slipping quietly into his own picture to watch the company march out.
High in the background hangs a shield, easy to miss in the gloom.
It bears the names of eighteen militiamen and is thought to have been added around 1715.
The Night Watch is not the original title.
As the varnish darkened over the years, the scene came to look like night, and the name first appears in a document of 1797.
It was originally a daytime scene.
In 1715, when it was moved to the town hall, it was trimmed on all four sides to fit between two doors.
The largest strip came off the left, taking two figures with it, and the pieces have never been found.
The painting was attacked with knives in 1911 and 1975, and with acid in 1990, and each time it was restored.
Since 2019, a major conservation project has carried on inside a glass room, in full view of visitors.
Step back and follow where the light lands.
It gathers on the captain, the lieutenant and the girl.
Among dozens of faces, Rembrandt used light to decide whom we see first.
